Index.meta_title: Inferon — see what every AI request really costs
Index.meta_description: A gateway that works with the OpenAI API. It measures, protects and routes your AI traffic, so you always see the real cost and stay inside your budget.

Hero.title: Know what every AI request <important>really costs</important>.
Hero.description: Inferon sits between your app and the AI providers. It measures each request, protects your budget and moves traffic to cheaper models — and your current OpenAI client keeps working unchanged.

Features.section_title: Everything you need to trust your AI spend
Features.section_description: A gateway that measures cost and stays out of your way. Your current OpenAI client keeps working.
Features.feature1_title: The real cost of each request
Features.feature1_description: Every request stores its token counts and what the provider charged, in exact dollars and cents — never a rounded estimate.
Features.feature2_description: Set a budget for each workspace. When it runs low, Inferon switches to a cheaper model instead of letting the bill run past the limit.
Features.feature3_description: Checks that the JSON a model sends back matches the shape you asked for, and fixes it. If it still fails, the request is retried on a stronger model.
Features.feature4_description: Point your client at /v1/chat/completions and keep your current SDK, keys and request formats.
Features.feature5_description: Create and revoke API keys for each workspace from the dashboard. Only a hash of each key is stored, never the key itself.
Features.feature6_description: People sign in with GitHub and get a signed session cookie. Teammates join by invite and use their own API keys.

ProvidersPage.title_bar_description: Use your own provider account. The gateway runs on your key.
ProvidersPage.empty: No provider yet — add one so requests have somewhere to go.
ProvidersPage.name: Name
ProvidersPage.key_note: Encrypted and never shown again. We keep only a masked hint.
ProvidersPage.owner_only: Only the workspace owner can manage providers.
ProvidersPage.error: Could not update providers. Please try again.
ProvidersPage.rotate_key_note: Leave blank to keep the current key. Enter a new one to replace it.
ProvidersPage.headers_note: One `Name: Value` per line. They are sent with every request to this provider.
ProvidersPage.models_error: Could not read the model list from this provider.
ProvidersPage.local_note: A model on your own network. Inference is free here, but the cloud must be able to reach this URL (use HTTPS if it is public). Only the endpoint you expose is used; the rest of your network stays private.

ProvidersPage.local_free: Free — runs on your own hardware

QualityPage.title_bar_description: How often answers were usable. This is worked out from the response itself, plus your thumbs up or down when you give them.
QualityPage.success_rate_help: Answers that were not empty and did not fail, refuse or get cut short.
QualityPage.empty_rate_help: A 200 response with no content. Usually the token budget was used up by the model’s reasoning.
QualityPage.error_rate_help: Failures at the provider, timeouts and gateway errors.
QualityPage.truncated_rate_help: The answer hit its max_tokens limit before it finished.
QualityPage.guard_fallback_rate_help: Structured output that did not match its schema and was retried on a stronger model.

RoutingPage.title_bar_description: Choose the order of models used when a request fails.
RoutingPage.help: When the main model fails for a reason worth retrying (a connection error, a 429 or a 5xx), Inferon tries the next model in the chain. A problem with the request itself (a 4xx) is never retried.
RoutingPage.primary_help: the model your request asks for
RoutingPage.empty: No fallback. A failing request just returns the error.
RoutingPage.owner_only: Only the workspace owner can change routing.
RoutingPage.error: Could not save routing. Please try again.
RoutingPage.tier_pairs_help: Send simple traffic that asks for an expensive model to a cheaper one you choose, including your own local model. Your pairs win over the built-in ones.
RoutingPage.tier_pairs_empty: No pairs. The built-in table applies (gpt-4o → gpt-4o-mini, deepseek-v4-pro → deepseek-flash).
RoutingPage.tier_pairs_inactive: inactive — one of the models is disabled
RoutingPage.tier_pairs_error: Could not save the pairs. Please try again.
RoutingPage.triggers_help: Each step lists what it handles. By default that is connection errors, 429s and 5xx. Add “checker” to a step only if a failed structured response should be retried there, instead of on the built-in model.
RoutingPage.audit_help: Who changed a routing, budget or payload setting, and when. Newest first. Entries are never edited or deleted.

ControlsPage.cheap_help: Used once 85% of the budget is spent.
ControlsPage.guard: Output checker (check and fix tool-call JSON)
ControlsPage.router: Automatic router (send simple requests to a cheaper model)
ControlsPage.threshold_help: Requests scoring below this go to the cheap model (0–1).
ControlsPage.owner_only: Only the workspace owner can change these controls.
ControlsPage.error: Could not save. Please try again.
ControlsPage.capture: Store raw prompts and answers (dataset pairs)
ControlsPage.capture_help: Off: costs, outcomes and totals are still recorded, but no prompt or answer is stored, so nothing can go into a dataset.
ControlsPage.retention_help: Older payloads are deleted by a periodic clean-up. 0 keeps them forever.
ControlsPage.lint_help: Advisory checks before a request is sent. They never change the request; they only record what looks wasteful and put a price on it. Choose the rules you want.

SettingsPage.title_bar_description: Your workspace in one place: connect a client, manage keys and members, and see who you are signed in as.
SettingsPage.connect_body: Create a key, point your SDK at the gateway and send your first request.
SettingsPage.related_body: Everything else that changes how requests are handled.
SettingsPage.keys_help: Create, check and revoke the keys your clients use. The full key is shown once.
SettingsPage.members_help: Invite teammates by GitHub login. They join as members the next time they sign in.
SettingsPage.connect_key_step_help: Your key proves who you are to the API. It is shown once, so copy it now.
SettingsPage.connect_create_key_failed: Could not create the key. Please try again.
SettingsPage.connect_key_once: This is the only time your key is shown. Copy it now:
SettingsPage.connect_model_help: The model id your first request calls. Pick one you enabled, or type your provider’s own id.
SettingsPage.connect_links_help: Models belong to the provider that serves them.

SpendReportPage.title_bar_description: Every dollar over the last {days} days, by model, provider, API key and system prompt.
SpendReportPage.transactions_help: A session is every request that shared one X-Inferon-Session-Id: an agent loop, a chat thread or a batch run.

AuditPage.title_bar_description: Six findings built from your last {days} days of traffic. Refreshes every 15 seconds.
AuditPage.no_traffic_title: No traffic in this window yet
AuditPage.no_traffic_body: Point your SDK at the Inferon gateway and this report fills itself in from your own requests.
AuditPage.affinity_requests: Requests that reused a cached prompt
AuditPage.f1_title: Models that are too big for the job
AuditPage.f1_desc: Expensive models answering tiny requests (under 100 input and 50 output tokens) that a cheaper model would answer just as well.
AuditPage.f2_desc: Expensive models used on plain text, with no tools, schema or structured output.
AuditPage.f3_desc: The same long prompt is sent again and again, but the provider cache is not saving you anything.
AuditPage.f4_desc: What the router and the fallback chain saved, compared with sending everything to the expensive model.
AuditPage.f5_desc: Which model, provider and key drove your spend.
AuditPage.f6_desc: Requests you paid for that came back empty, refused, cut short or failed — and why.
AuditPage.share_body: Create a read-only link. It shows the six findings and never your prompts, keys or answers. You can revoke it at any time.
AuditPage.share_once: Copy this link now. It is shown only once.
AuditPage.public_body: A read-only report built from live traffic. Refreshes every 15 seconds.
AuditPage.invalid_body: It may have been revoked, or the address is wrong.

DatasetsPage.title_bar_description: Checked examples from your real traffic: how many there are, what they cost, why the rest did not qualify, and a JSONL download.
DatasetsPage.grouping_help: Task type groups prompts that mean the same thing. The hash groups prompts that are byte-for-byte identical.
DatasetsPage.spend_help: Across the window, including traffic that was excluded
DatasetsPage.empty: No stored pairs yet. Traffic qualifies when the answer is stored and there is no thumbs-down. Check that payload storage is on.
DatasetsPage.purge_confirm: Delete every stored payload now? Costs are kept, but pairs are not.
DatasetsPage.purge_error: Could not delete. Please try again.
DatasetsPage.clusters_help: Prompt groups, either by hash or by meaning, depending on how you group.
DatasetsPage.excluded_help: Traffic that did not qualify: a missing answer, a thumbs-down or a failed request.

PruningPanel.help: Optional. Exact duplicate turns are removed before the request is sent. If you set a token budget, the oldest turns beyond it are dropped too. Tool definitions, the system prompt and the last turn are never touched. A request with a schema contract is never rewritten. A small share of requests is sent without pruning so you can measure the effect, and a drop in quality turns pruning off automatically.
PruningPanel.budget_placeholder: e.g. 8000 — leave blank for no limit
PruningPanel.budget_help: Estimated as characters ÷ 4. The oldest turns go first, after the system prompt and the last turn.
PruningPanel.holdout_help: Share of requests sent without pruning, so you can compare. Limited to 50%.
PruningPanel.owner_only: Only the workspace owner can change pruning.
PruningPanel.error: Could not save pruning. Please try again.

EvalsPage.title_bar_description: Test a model against a fixed set of good answers from your own traffic, and check a change before you trust it.
EvalsPage.gold_help: A gold set is a frozen copy of verified examples: the exact inputs and their reference answers. Later clean-ups or pruning cannot change what a run measured.
EvalsPage.no_gold: No gold set yet. Pin one from your qualified examples.
EvalsPage.run_help: Every run is limited by case count and spend, and never touches your production totals, budgets or routing.
EvalsPage.gate_help: Compare a challenger with a baseline. With fewer than 20 scored cases, or an unfinished run, there is no verdict.
EvalsPage.need_two_runs: Run at least two models to compare them.
EvalsPage.owner_only: Only the workspace owner can run evals.
EvalsPage.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.

PromptsPage.title_bar_description: Name a prompt, see every version your traffic has produced, and compare two of them. Read-only: naming a prompt never edits it or deletes a trace.
PromptsPage.name: Name
PromptsPage.hash_placeholder: the system prompt hash, from a dataset group
PromptsPage.label: Name this version
PromptsPage.none: No named prompts yet. Name a content hash to start tracking versions.
PromptsPage.content_unavailable: This workspace does not store payloads, so there is no text to compare. The counts still work.
PromptsPage.owner_only: Only the workspace owner can name a prompt.
PromptsPage.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.

RuntimePage.title_bar_description: Is the gateway fast? Here is its own overhead, the promise it is measured against, the end-to-end latency around it, and where it slows down by time and model. The prompt size beside a number is the one it was measured at.
RuntimePage.claim_p95: 95th percentile overhead under 5 ms (catches a cache slowdown)
RuntimePage.claim_window: Measured on this build: the last {hours} h ({samples} sample(s), median {observed} at a median prompt of {tokens} tokens). The cards above describe the window you selected.
RuntimePage.claim_note: Gateway time is measured from the moment the request body has finished arriving to just before it is sent to the provider, so the client's upload, the provider's time and the response body are all excluded. Warm requests arrive within the cache window; the first request after an idle period also has to load the config.
RuntimePage.heatmap_help: 95th-percentile total latency and error rate for each model in each period. A dot means no traffic, not a fast day. Every cell prints its value; the tint is only a hint.
RuntimePage.no_samples: No requests measured in this window.
RuntimePage.overhead_help: The gateway's own work: from the moment your request has finished arriving to just before it is sent to the provider. The time you spend sending the body is not included — a slow upload is your network, not our latency.
RuntimePage.under_1ms_help: Share of measured requests whose own overhead stayed under the 1 ms claim.
RuntimePage.samples_help: Requests with a measured overhead in this window. This is the base for every number on this page.
RuntimePage.total_help: End to end: from the start of the request to the last byte of the response.
RuntimePage.ttft_help: From the start of the request to the first token of the response.
RuntimePage.legend_healthy: No tint: under 5% errors and a slowest 5% under 3 s
RuntimePage.legend_degraded: Light tint: 5% or more errors, or the slowest 5% over 3 s
RuntimePage.legend_failing: Dark tint: 20% or more errors, or the slowest 5% over 10 s
RuntimePage.legend_empty: dot: no traffic in that period
RuntimePage.upload_beside: clients took a median {ms} ms to send the body (not counted above)
RuntimePage.no_small_prompts: no prompts under {tokens} tokens in this window
RuntimePage.small_only: measured over prompts of {tokens} tokens or fewer
RuntimePage.claim_basis: Judged only on prompts of {tokens} tokens or fewer — the size the 1 ms claim was calibrated on. Bigger prompts have their own measured cost, in the table below.
RuntimePage.bands_empty: No requests measured yet in this window. The clock starts when the request body has arrived, so only traffic after the 2026-11-08 change is counted here.
RuntimePage.bands_note: Upload is the median time clients spent sending the body. It is never counted as gateway time: a slow link is not a slow proxy. An empty band is hidden rather than shown as zero.
RuntimePage.era_note: Gateway figures here count only requests measured since {since}, when the clock began starting from the completed body. {count} earlier requests are excluded: their figure included the time the client spent uploading.

PayloadsPage.title_bar_description: What happens to prompts and answers: whether they are stored and for how long, what the linters found, what pruning removed, and which kinds of personal data were detected. Counts only, never a value.
PayloadsPage.capture_off_help: Payloads are not stored. Only cost, speed and outcomes are kept.
PayloadsPage.capture_help: Whether raw prompts and answers are stored at all, and for how long. Costs, speed and outcomes are always kept.
PayloadsPage.lint_help: Two passes: one before the request is sent (repeated prompts, oversized schemas, boilerplate, duplicate turns) and the cost rules once the trace arrives. Both are advisory: the payload is sent unchanged.
PayloadsPage.pruning_help: Optional rewriting of repeated context, with a comparison group so you can measure the effect on quality. A request with a schema contract is never rewritten.
PayloadsPage.pruning_off: Pruning is off. Every payload is sent unchanged.
PayloadsPage.pii_help: Pattern checks on stored payloads. Counts only: a matched value is never recorded. This is not a compliance guarantee.
PayloadsPage.lint_coverage_help: Requests the pre-flight linter actually inspected, out of all traffic in the window.
PayloadsPage.lint_findings_help: Pre-flight findings in this window, and what their waste was priced at.
PayloadsPage.prune_removed_help: Requests whose context was rewritten by the pruning policy.

ErrorClass.upstream_429_help: It reached the provider and was refused. It still counts on your provider bill. Add a fallback step that handles 429, or slow down.
ErrorClass.upstream_5xx_help: The provider returned an error. A fallback step that handles 5xx answers instead of returning the failure.
ErrorClass.client_4xx_help: The request itself was wrong for that provider — usually a model name it does not serve, or a field it does not accept.
ErrorClass.inferon_4xx_help: No provider could take it: none configured, the model is disabled, or your key hit a limit. Nothing was billed.
ErrorClass.rate_limited_help: Requests or tokens per minute for this key. Raise it on the key, or give each service its own key.
ErrorClass.inferon_5xx_help: Our side failed before a model answered. Retry once; if it repeats, report the trace id.
ErrorClass.transport: The provider could not be reached
ErrorClass.transport_help: Nothing was sent: wrong address, TLS, firewall or a timeout. Test the provider from the gateway.
ErrorClass.timeout_help: The connection was open but no answer arrived in time. A faster model or a shorter prompt helps.
ErrorClass.guard: The output checker refused the answer
ErrorClass.guard_help: The answer did not match the schema the request asked for.
ErrorClass.client_abort_help: The connection closed before the answer finished, so there is no completion to bill.

Outcome.flushed_help: The structured answer matched the contract and was served.
Outcome.fallback_help: The answer did not match, so the request was replayed on a stronger model and that answer was served.
Outcome.fallback_failed: Retry on a stronger model failed
Outcome.fallback_failed_help: Both answers missed the contract, so the client received the failure.
